Reporting to the Senior Marketing Director, KIND, the Sr. Brand Manager, Innovation owns what KIND launches next. The role is accountable for the brand’s 18-month to 3-year innovation pipeline end to end: the consumer needs the brand should solve for, where it plays next, the propositions that get it there, the products that make them real, and the stage gates that decide what moves forward and what stops. Every launch starts with a real consumer problem, and this role is the brand’s deepest expert on who the KIND consumer is, what they want from snacking, and where the unmet needs are. This role leads a team of a Brand Manager and a Senior Associate Brand Manager, each owning a platform, and holds the earliest-stage bets personally until they earn an owner. The role works shoulder to shoulder with Consumer Research and R&D from the first consumer question to the final formulation, and hands the Core team launches that are ready to win.
What will be your key responsibilities?
Innovation Strategy & Portfolio Direction
Own the KIND innovation strategy: where the brand plays next across formats, occasions and adjacencies, grounded in a deep understanding of the consumer, their snacking needs and occasions, category dynamics and the brand platform.
Build and maintain the brand’s innovation insight foundation: who the KIND consumer is and could be, the jobs they hire snacks to do, the tensions and unmet needs in the category, and where KIND has the right to play.
Represent KIND innovation to Better For You leadership and global markets, building platforms that can travel and bringing market and consumer learning back into the pipeline.
Bring the Accelerator way of working into the brand: founder-style ownership, fast and cheap experiments, clear kill criteria, and the willingness to scale hard when something proves out.
Pipeline Management & Business Case Development
Build and own the 18-month to 3-year pipeline, sequencing launches against capacity, investment and the commercial calendar so the brand always has news coming.
Own the stage-gate and Integrated Business Planning (IBP) steps and make the portfolio calls on what enters, accelerates, parks or stops. Decide early, decide with consumer evidence, defend the decision.
Build the business case for every launch, volume, margin, investment, incrementality and return, and partner with Finance to secure funding.
Own the early-stage bets personally from consumer insight through concept and validation until each passes a gate and earns an owner or stops.
Product Design & Development
Write propositions that start with the consumer: the problem, the person, the reason KIND wins, and the evidence that it will.
Lead product design across every component: formulation, format, pack structure and graphics, nutrition, taste and texture, naming and claims, so the product delivers the proposition in the hand.
Set the learning plan with Consumer Research for each platform, from concept screens through sensory and in-market validation, and stay close to the consumer throughout, in the research and in the field.
Partner with R&D as co-owners of the product on cost, capacity and ingredient trade-offs, and own the standard a KIND product must meet before it launches.
Launch Readiness & Cross-Functional Leadership
Hand each launch to the Core, Equity & GTM team at a defined point of go-to-market readiness, with proposition, product, business case and launch plan complete, and stay accountable for the first-year read.
Lead the innovation workstream across R&D, Supply, Finance, Insights, Category, Sales and Omni as one plan with shared milestones and KPIs.
Build and manage the external partnerships the pipeline depends on.
Talent & Capability
Lead and develop the Brand Manager and Senior Associate Brand Manager, giving each real platform ownership and cross-functional leadership.
Build innovation capability into the brand: faster concept testing, AI-enabled insight and ideation tools, and a repeatable path from idea to gate.
Bring the outside in: consumer and cultural trends, category, competitor and adjacent innovation, and what the brand can learn from how others are winning.
What are we looking for?
Undergraduate degree required, preferably in Marketing, Business Administration or a technical discipline. MBA or other graduate degree preferred.
8+ years of progressive experience in Marketing, Brand Management or Innovation within CPG, with at least 4 years in an innovation role on a scaled consumer brand. Challenger brand, start-up or growth business experience is a strong asset.
Deep consumer understanding: has built innovation from a real consumer insight rather than a product idea, is fluent in qualitative and quantitative research, and can turn what consumers say and do into a sharp, ownable proposition.
Has taken a product from insight through concept, development, business case and launch, with clear accountability for the result in market.
Has run a multi-year pipeline and stage-gate process, including making and defending kill decisions.
Has led product design across formulation, format, pack, nutrition and sensory in deep partnership with R&D and Consumer Research.
Has managed external partners such as co-manufacturers, ingredient and technology suppliers or research institutions.
Builds business cases that hold up: sizes the opportunity, models volume, margin and investment, and can defend the number with senior stakeholders.
Has managed and developed people and led cross-functional teams without direct authority in a matrixed environment.
Entrepreneurial by instinct, with a bias for action, comfort with ambiguity and curiosity for how data and AI-enabled tools can change the speed and quality of innovation.

title: Senior Data Scientist for Copilot Evals
description:
Overview
CADET (Customer and Analytics Driven Evals Team) is building a customer-grounded quality system for Copilot. Our mission is to rapidly identify the customer scenarios that matter most, represent them faithfully in evaluation and learning assets, run quality gates continuously, and turn every important failure into reusable product and model improvements. We bring together DSAT and other product signals, deep customer engagements to create representative eval sets. Operating in a fast-paced environment, we connect customer grounded quality issues with quality teams to advance Copilot quality and product innovation.   We are looking for a Senior Data Scientist to build the measurement and decision system that determines where CADET invests and whether Copilot is improving for the customers and intents that matter most. You will combine DSAT, usage, customer engagement, product feedback, evaluation, and other quality signals to create a representation- and coverage-aware view of customer quality. You will define the taxonomies, metrics, prioritization models, analyses, and reporting mechanisms that turn a fragmented signal landscape into clear decisions. You will synthesize quality opportunities, investigate loss patterns, shape evaluation portfolios, and ensure recurring quality gates reflect real customer experiences rather than static benchmarks.   Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
Build and operate a data-driven prioritization framework for CADET quality forums and partner teams that combines DSAT, customer impact, usage, severity, strategic importance, representation, and current evaluation coverage to guide quality investments.
Define and maintain intent, sub-intent, customer scenario, coverage, and loss-pattern taxonomies that can be used consistently across signal intake, triage, evaluation, and reporting.
Measure how well evaluation portfolios represent production traffic, customer segments, workflow complexity, locales, grounding paths, and material failure modes.
Identify underrepresented customers, intents, scenarios, and loss patterns, and translate those gaps into evaluation and data-collection priorities.
Design quality gates for top intents and top customers, including success thresholds, segmentation, run cadence, escalation criteria, and reporting.
Build recurring scorecards that connect offline evaluation movement with online measures such as DSAT, task completion, retries, abandonment, and escalation; detect meaningful quality changes; and alert accountable owners when action is required.
Analyze offline-online agreement, evaluation freshness, regression coverage, grader reliability, and quality movement over time.
Develop sampling, weighting, deduplication, clustering, and trend-detection approaches for noisy customer and product signals using resource- and performance-optimized data-analysis solutions that make effective use of CPU, GPU, and platform capacity.
Use causal and experimental methods where appropriate to distinguish correlation, attribution, and treatment impact, and translate the findings into concrete product, model, data, and evaluation investment decisions.
Partner to translate customer evidence into valid task distributions, datasets, metrics, and reward signals and to encode metrics, taxonomies, data-quality checks, and reporting into automated pipelines.
Leverage team signals from customer engagements to understand workflows, business impact, expected outcomes, and gaps hidden by aggregate metrics; produce clear recommendations for product, model, data, and evaluation investments; and communicate them to senior leaders.
Establish solid practices for data provenance, privacy, responsible use, reproducibility, and metric governance.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
Doctorate in Data Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Econometrics, Economics, Operations Research, Computer Science, or related field AND 1+ year(s) data-science experience (e.g., managing structured and unstructured data, applying statistical techniques and reporting results) OR Master's Degree in Data Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Econometrics, Economics, Operations Research, Computer Science, or related field AND 3+ years data-science experience (e.g., managing structured and unstructured data, applying statistical techniques and reporting results)
OR Bachelor's Degree in Data Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Econometrics, Economics, Operations Research, Computer Science, or related field AND 5+ years data-science experience (e.g., managing structured and unstructured data, applying statistical techniques and reporting results)
OR equivalent experience.
Preferred Qualifications:
Solid experience using data to shape product strategy and decisions in a complex, high-scale product or platform environment.
Expertise in SQL and at least one analytical programming language such as Python or R.
Solid foundation in statistical analysis, experimentation, sampling, segmentation, measurement, and data visualization.
Experience integrating noisy quantitative and qualitative signals into actionable prioritization or measurement frameworks.
Ability to define durable metrics and taxonomies, explain their limitations, and prevent misleading interpretation.
Demonstrated ability to communicate complex analysis clearly to technical, product, and executive audiences.
Experience with AI product quality, LLM or agent evaluation, DSAT or customer feedback analysis, experimentation, or model telemetry.
Experience designing representative datasets, coverage models, quality scorecards, or regression portfolios.
Experience with clustering, text analytics, embeddings, classification, anomaly detection, or other methods for mining unstructured feedback.
Experience connecting offline evaluation results with online product and customer outcomes.
Experience working directly with enterprise customers, researchers, product managers, and engineers.
Familiarity with responsible AI, privacy-preserving analysis, data governance, and customer-data handling.

OpenAI's infrastructure teams design, build, activate, and operate the critical systems that support large-scale AI compute. Field Service Engineering partners across design, construction, commissioning, site operations, hardware operations, and equipment providers to turn complex infrastructure into safe, reliable, and serviceable systems.

About the Role

We are seeking a senior, field service engineer to build the technical operating model responsible for critical electrical and mechanical infrastructure across our data center portfolio. This is a field-oriented electrical & mechanical engineering role, not a traditional facilities operations position. You will combine deep systems understanding in data center power and cooling systems to aid in SOO, design, maintenance & operability, troubleshooting and other engineering related responsibility around key equipment.  The role will include leveraging training and experience to establish standards, develop people, coordinate vendors, and drive issues from design, first principles, first signals through verified resolution. Remote - travel 50%

 - Lead field support for startup, commissioning, troubleshooting, repair, and reliability improvement across critical data center infrastructure.

 - Serve as the senior technical owner for transformers, switchgear, UPS systems, generators, PDUs, protection and controls, chillers, cooling towers, pumps, CDUs, CRAH units, and associated control systems.

 - Diagnose complex failures across power, cooling, controls, and hardware interfaces; distinguish symptoms from root causes and drive corrective actions through validation.

 - Build the field service operating model, including staffing recommendations, coverage, escalation paths, response expectations, spare-parts strategy, documentation, and performance metrics.

 - Aid in hiring, development, and coaching other field service engineers and technicians while creating a culture of safety, technical rigor, accountability, and continuous learning.

 - Partner with design, construction, commissioning, site operations, and hardware teams to improve maintainability, readiness, and lifecycle reliability.

 - Manage OEM and service-provider relationships, technical escalations, repair plans, warranties, and sustained corrective action.

 - Translate field learning into design feedback, preventive maintenance improvements, training, and reusable standards.

Qualifications

 - 8+ years of hands-on experience supporting critical electrical, mechanical, or electromechanical infrastructure in data centers, industrial facilities, utilities, manufacturing, or similarly complex environments.

 - Deep technical expertise in at least one discipline, electrical or mechanical, with demonstrated ability to troubleshoot across electromechanical and controls boundaries.

 - Experience building, leading, or materially developing a field engineering, service, maintenance, or technician team.

 - Demonstrated success leading high-severity troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and reliability improvement.

 - Ability to read and use one-line diagrams, schematics, P&IDs, sequence-of-operations documents, control diagrams, equipment manuals, and commissioning records.

 - Strong safety judgment and experience working under formal energization, isolation, maintenance, and change-control procedures.

 - Ability to travel up to 50% and support planned or urgent field activity when required.

title: Fire Protection Engineer
description:

OpenAI's Industrial Compute organization delivers the infrastructure that powers frontier AI models. Within Infrastructure Delivery, we turn engineering concepts into safe, reliable, and operational AI campuses by working across design, construction, utilities, commissioning, operations, and external partners.

The fire protection function establishes the life-safety and property-protection strategy for these campuses. The team connects code requirements and engineering standards to practical design, construction, testing, incident readiness, and long-term operations.

About the Role

We are seeking a Fire Protection Engineer to lead owner-side fire and life-safety engineering across large-scale data center programs. You will establish design criteria, review complex fire protection systems, coordinate with authorities and delivery partners, and ensure that fire and life-safety requirements remain clear from early design through construction, commissioning, and operational handover.

This role requires strong technical judgment across detection, alarm, suppression, smoke control, water supply, emergency response, and code compliance. You will work closely with engineering, construction, safety, security, commissioning, and operations teams to resolve risks quickly without compromising life safety, reliability, or schedule.

Key Responsibilities

 - Develop and maintain fire protection and life-safety design criteria, technical standards, and review requirements for self-build data center campuses.

 - Review fire protection drawings, specifications, code analyses, fire and life-safety narratives, hydraulic calculations, equipment submittals, and sequences of operation across all project phases.

 - Provide owner-side engineering direction for fire detection and alarm, automatic suppression, fire pumps and water storage, smoke control, emergency communication, and related life-safety systems.

 - Integrate fire protection requirements with architectural, structural, electrical, mechanical, controls, security, hardware, and operational systems.

 - Partner with code officials, authorities having jurisdiction, insurers, consultants, contractors, and equipment vendors to resolve code interpretations and approval risks.

 - Support constructability reviews, RFIs, submittals, field inspections, deficiency resolution, and change management during active construction.

 - Define commissioning, integrated-system testing, acceptance, turnover, and operational-readiness criteria for fire and life-safety systems.

 - Assess fire and life-safety risks associated with high-density compute, battery and energy-storage systems, generators and fuel systems, utility infrastructure, cooling systems, hazardous materials, and construction activities.

 - Support incident response, root-cause reviews, corrective actions, and lessons learned, translating operational findings into improved designs and standards.

 - Maintain clear records of design decisions, code positions, approvals, testing results, open risks, and turnover requirements.

 - Travel regularly to project sites to support design reviews, field execution, testing, commissioning, and operational readiness.

Qualifications

 - Bachelor's degree in Fire Protection Engineering or a related engineering discipline, or equivalent practical experience delivering fire and life-safety systems.

 - 8+ years of fire protection engineering experience supporting data centers, industrial facilities, advanced manufacturing, energy infrastructure, or other mission-critical environments.

 - Strong knowledge of applicable building and fire codes and standards, including IBC, IFC, NFPA requirements, and local authority approval processes.

 - Technical depth in fire alarm and detection, water-based suppression, special-hazard suppression, fire pumps and water supply, smoke control, egress, and integrated life-safety systems.

 - Experience reviewing fire protection designs, specifications, hydraulic calculations, equipment submittals, testing procedures, and commissioning results.

 - Demonstrated ability to work with authorities having jurisdiction, engineering consultants, contractors, insurers, vendors, and internal stakeholders.

 - Experience resolving field issues and design changes while maintaining clear code compliance, safety, quality, schedule, and documentation.

 - Strong written and verbal communication, sound engineering judgment, and the ability to create clarity when requirements or ownership are ambiguous.

 - Professional Engineer licensure in Fire Protection Engineering, or the ability to obtain licensure in relevant jurisdictions.

 - Experience with hyperscale data centers, high-density compute environments, or global multi-site infrastructure programs.

 - Experience with battery rooms, energy-storage systems, generator plants, fuel systems, high-voltage substations, or other campus utility infrastructure.

 - Familiarity with performance-based design, fire and smoke modeling, quantitative risk assessment, or fire-hazard analysis.

 - Experience leading integrated testing and coordinating fire alarm, suppression, controls, security, mechanical, and electrical interfaces.

 - Experience developing reusable standards, design templates, commissioning requirements, and incident-prevention programs across multiple sites.

title: Motion Designer
description:
About the Team

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a Motion Designer to help tell the stories behind our research. You’ll translate complex ideas, emerging capabilities, and the work of our researchers into clear, engaging motion across films, launches, demos, and other communications.

Working within the creative team, you’ll partner with Research, Brand, and production teams to shape work from early concepts through final delivery. You’ll help determine what a story needs visually, explore different approaches, and bring those ideas to life through thoughtful design and animation.

This is a hands-on role for someone with strong motion craft, curiosity about unfamiliar subjects, and the ability to find a compelling visual approach when the brief is still taking shape. You’ll contribute to how OpenAI’s research is expressed in motion, developing original work and reusable approaches that help the team build on what it learns.

In this role, you will:

 - Develop motion concepts for research stories, working with creative partners and subject matter experts to understand the ideas and identify how best to communicate them.

 - Design and produce high-quality 2D and 3D motion for research films, launches, demos, and supporting content.

 - Apply and extend OpenAI’s visual and motion language, balancing consistency with the needs of each story.

 - Take work from visual exploration, storyboards, and animatics through animation, compositing, and final delivery.

 - Collaborate closely with designers, filmmakers, editors, producers, and researchers, bringing a motion perspective into the creative process early.

 - Translate technical or abstract concepts into visual sequences that are accessible to a broad audience while preserving the meaning of the underlying work.

 - Work with producers to scope projects, communicate dependencies, and maintain a high standard of craft as priorities and timelines evolve.

 - Present work clearly, explain creative decisions, and incorporate feedback from creative and technical partners.

 - Develop reusable assets, templates, and workflows where they improve quality and make recurring work easier to produce.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - 7+ years of experience in motion design across films, campaigns, launches, or other narrative work.

 - A strong portfolio demonstrating design judgment, animation craft, and the ability to carry an idea from concept through finished execution.

 - The ability to explore an open-ended brief, propose a clear creative direction, and refine it through collaboration.

 - Proficiency in After Effects and experience with Cinema 4D or comparable 3D tools, alongside editing and compositing workflows.

 - Comfort working in Figma and sharing work across design and production teams.

 - A strong understanding of typography, composition, timing, rhythm, and visual storytelling.

 - Experience making complex or unfamiliar subjects understandable through design and motion.

 - Experience working with subject matter experts and incorporating technical feedback without losing clarity or creative quality.

 - Curiosity about AI and research, and a willingness to learn enough about a subject to represent it thoughtfully.

title: Network Infrastructure Lead
description:
About the Role

Lead OpenAI’s site network infrastructure delivery, coordinating the physical installation and readiness of network systems with the central network team and contracted installation providers.

You will be OpenAI’s accountable on-site lead for physical network infrastructure construction and deployment, directing and overseeing the work of general contractors, specialist contractors and other service providers within your discipline. You will combine practical subject-matter depth with hands-on field leadership, managing contracted support to deliver safe, high-quality work to the integrated construction plan.

Reporting and scope

Report to the Site Construction Manager, who reports through the applicable project-management leadership. Maintain functional alignment with the Network Infrastructure leader and central network engineering team.

Own day-to-day discipline execution and contractor performance within the assigned site scope and delegated authority. Coordinate priorities and interfaces through the Site Construction Manager; escalate material cost, schedule, design and acceptance decisions to the appropriate owners.

This is a senior site delivery role, suited to an experienced superintendent, supervisor, manager or trade lead. Accountability is for an assigned discipline and site work packages. Site assignment, duration and any shared coverage follow project phase, workload and the staffing plan; effective on-site coverage is required during critical activities.

Key Responsibilities

 - Manage structured-cabling contractors, fiber installers, network installation partners and other service providers against the site delivery plan.

 - Translate approved network designs into executable field packages and coordinate bills of materials, material availability and installation sequencing with the central network team.

 - Oversee pathways, duct banks and building-entry interfaces, fiber and copper cabling, racks, patching, labeling and network-equipment installation as applicable.

 - Direct fiber and cabling quality assurance, review test results and traceability, and drive correction of defective or incomplete installations.

 - Coordinate power, cooling, space and physical access readiness with electrical, mechanical and CSLA leads and hardware deployment teams.

 - Coordinate network provisioning, connectivity validation and handover with authorized network engineering and operations teams; maintain accurate installation and as-built records.

 - Typically 8–10 years of large-scale data center network deployment, structured cabling, physical-layer installation or infrastructure delivery, with demonstrated field and contractor leadership. Equivalent depth of practical delivery experience will be considered.

 - Strong understanding of physical data center network topologies, network components, bills of materials, rack constraints and installation sequencing; translate approved designs into executable field plans.

 - Deep practical knowledge of fiber and copper plant installation, trunks, panels, terminations, cleaning, labeling and cable administration, including routing diversity and pathway separation.

 - Ability to oversee and assess port-to-port verification, continuity, optical power and optical time-domain reflectometer (OTDR) testing; troubleshoot field installation and mapping discrepancies and verify remediation.

 - Comfort with ticket-based execution, change control, incident escalation and documentation workflows that make network installation repeatable and auditable.

 - Demonstrated ability to lead contractors and service providers through changing site conditions, set clear deliverables and acceptance criteria, and resolve performance gaps across organizations without relying on direct reporting authority.

ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.

At S&C, we are dedicated to providing competitive and equitable compensation for all our team members, with a commitment to transparency in our pay practices. Join Our Team as a Finisher!
Are you passionate about metal finishing? S&C Electric Company is seeking a dynamic individual to coordinate our metal finishing function. As a finisher, you’ll be crucial in ensuring smooth operations and supporting our diverse team. The Finishing System is a process designed to pre-treat metal (i.e., powder coat and liquid paint) to protect it from the environment. You will work in a production environment, engage in continuous productive activity and must meet requirements within predetermined time constraints. Tasks require the use of both hands and arms on a repetitive basis for a full range of motion.
Key Responsibilities:
Identify parts from blueprints to verify that they are properly tagged.
Have the ability to use simple material handling equipment such as powered walking stackers, storage trucks and pallet trucks.
Use simple measuring equipment such as tape measures.
Have the ability to learn proper grinding procedures to smooth welds and remove scratches from steel parts and enclosures.
Hanging of parts weighing up to 200 lbs. on an overhead conveyor using material handling equipment.
Reacting to system alarms and basic sanding procedures.
The work in this area is physically demanding and requires the ability to sustain a continuous work pace for extended periods.
What you’ll Need To Succeed:
A working knowledge of shop math.
Ability to follow specific instructions and procedures.
Requirements:
High School Diploma
Physical demands:
Standing: All tasks are performed in a standing position with intermittent walking.
Lifting: Frequent lifting of items ranging in weight from 5 lbs. to 50 lbs.
Walking: Occasional walking moderate distances (less than 1/8 mile).
Carrying: Frequent carrying of items ranging in weight from 5 lbs. to 25 lbs.
Pushing: Occasional pushing of motorized material handling carts with loaded weights up to 1000 lbs.
Pulling: Occasional pulling of motorized material handling carts with loaded weights up to 1000 lbs.
Bending: Frequent bending and crouching to safely lift parts of various sizes and shapes.
Reaching: Continuous full range of motion from above the shoulders to below the knees.
Handling: Continuous handling of parts ranging in weight from 5 lbs. to 50 lbs.
Other: Respirator certification required.

Experience operating, setting up, or troubleshooting robotic welding equipment.

High school diploma or equivalent (GED)
3+ years of demonstrated experience in a welding role in a manufacturing, automotive, or related environment.
Strong knowledge of welding techniques, metallurgy, welding symbols, and the properties of metals used in fabrication and assembly.
Knowledge of safety standards related to welding and metalworking.
Ability to pass a welding skills test.
Understanding of welding equipment maintenance and troubleshooting.
Ability to perform MIG, stick, and flux-cored arc welding techniques.
Proficient in reading and interpreting moderately complex blueprints, drawings, and specifications.
Good attention to detail to ensure precision in welding tasks.
Excellent hand-eye coordination and manual dexterity.
Ability to set up, operate, and maintain welding equipment and tools.

Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Tempus is on a mission to create the world’s largest integrated dataset of clinical and molecular data. We believe that, through data, we can make a lasting contribution to cancer research and treatment. At Tempus, products are owned and developed by small, autonomous teams of developers, designers, data scientists, and product managers who work together to build a platform that is both nimble and innovative.

As Senior Manager, Software Engineering, you will lead and mentor a small team of data engineers and data architects, and you will own the enterprise data model and the reliability of the data it represents. You will design how clinical records, genomics, next-generation sequencing (NGS) laboratory data, and radiology data are integrated, and you will ensure that the data are accurate, traceable, and suitable for critical applications such as machine learning and clinical decision-making.
You will establish modeling standards, implement quality gates in data pipelines, and develop the team through design review, code review, and ongoing coaching. You will use development tools assisted by artificial intelligence (AI) to accelerate design, testing, and delivery.
What You Will Do
Lead and mentor a small team of data engineers and data architects by conducting design and code reviews, providing technical guidance, and fostering a culture of excellence in data architecture and data quality.
Own and evolve an enterprise data model with engineers, product managers, scientists, and operators, integrating structured data from clinical records, genomics, the NGS laboratory, and radiology across relational and NoSQL data stores. Author and maintain entity-relationship diagrams, data dictionaries, API specifications, and data-translation documentation at the conceptual, logical, and physical levels.
Apply modern data architecture best practices and patterns, and teach modeling standards, including third normal form, dimensional (star schema) design, and established healthcare data model standards such as FHIR, OMOP, and related standards.
Evaluate the completeness of source-system models and partner data through profiling, and resolve structural inconsistencies before they reach downstream consumers.
Design observability for the data ecosystem with BigQuery, dbt, Elementary, and Grafana, including monitors, alerts, dashboards, lineage, and traceability back to source systems.
Partner with product managers and engineering leads to prioritize the backlog, estimate work, and translate complex requirements into actionable technical tasks. Advance the use of AI-assisted development, including Cursor, Claude, and GitHub Copilot, to accelerate modeling, testing, refactoring, and pipeline development.

You have a record of leading and mentoring a small team of data engineers and data architects, of setting standards, and of guiding design in a fast-paced environment. You can translate gaps in the data model and in data quality into clear recommendations for engineers, scientists, and other stakeholders.

You have applied modern data architecture best practices and patterns, and you can guide a team in their use. You have strong experience with third normal form (3NF) and dimensional (star schema) modeling; with established healthcare data model standards such as FHIR, OMOP, and related standards; and with modeling tools such as Erwin, Vertabelo, or Lucidchart.
You understand ETL/ELT and business intelligence (BI) architectures, and you can explain the long-term implications of choosing among relational, massively parallel processing (MPP), and NoSQL technologies. You have architected solutions across more than one of these technologies.
You have practical experience with data observability (for example, Elementary and Grafana) and with profiling and correlation analysis to identify data-integrity problems.
You have domain experience in healthcare and next-generation sequencing, including clinical and genomic data.
Preferred
Deep knowledge of Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and BigQuery architecture.
Experience modeling NGS data output.
Experience in implementing master data, reference data, or metadata management.
Why Join Tempus
You will work at the intersection of software engineering and cancer research. In this role, you will lead a small team of data engineers and data architects and shape the data model and quality systems that make Tempus data reliable enough for research and clinical use.

What you will gain
This role offers broad exposure to global accounting operations, cross-functional decision-making, and opportunities to improve systems and processes in a public-company environment.

Fixed Asset & Lease Accounting

Research transactions, resolve accounting questions, and perform financial analysis for U.S. and international subsidiaries.
Communicate conclusions clearly and work across functions, time zones, and levels of the organization to bring issues to resolution.

Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate, and strengthen accounting processes; contribute to system implementations and other finance initiatives.

Solid knowledge of U.S. GAAP, with practical experience applying ASC 360 and ASC 842.
Experience using an ERP and fixed asset subledger; Oracle experience is a plus.
Experience with lease accounting software; LeaseCalcs or a comparable platform is preferred.
Strong analytical, research, and problem-solving skills with consistent attention to detail and data quality.
Ability to prioritize competing demands, meet close and reporting deadlines, and take ownership through resolution.
Clear, concise written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with diverse stakeholders.
Preferred

Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and experience working with large data sets, reconciliations, and account rollforwards.
Experience supporting SOX controls and internal or external audits.
Experience improving accounting processes, supporting system enhancements, or using automation to reduce manual work.
